kit/nav — pathfinding adapters

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Query and follow a pathAPIWorked example: cavecrawl (examples/cavecrawl)Navigation constraints

kit/nav queries Godot’s 2D and 3D navigation maps and returns positions in Kit’s [3]f32 format. Use it when an AI character needs a route around scene obstacles. Godot owns the navigation meshes, region synchronization, and path search.

Path queries read the live NavigationServer, which cannot restore a historical mesh for replay. Run them from a non-resimulating authority pass: a cooperative host tick or a simulation-lane @(gd_step = "authority") world pass. Do not query from @(gd_tick), an everywhere @(gd_step), or a frame-clock callback. A historical tick queried against the current mesh can choose a different route and change every subsequent movement step.

Before querying, call pass_never_resims() in the enclosing scope. Path queries assert that this declaration is active. The declaration records the caller’s scheduling requirement; it does not prove that the caller is in the right pass. The simulation guide describes the same restriction for engine casts. Following an already recorded path with next_point and movement helpers is pure math, provided the path and cursor used for replay are also available.

Query and follow a path#

Declare the query scope, request the path, then select a waypoint:

Odin
knav.pass_never_resims()                                    // scoped, closes itself
path := knav.path_2d(self.owner, from, to, context.temp_allocator)
goal, ok := knav.next_point(path, &self.path_idx, my_pos, reach = 8)

When ok is true, the host’s AI can move toward goal with kit/ai’s step_toward. Both adapters return [3]f32; 2D positions use xy with z zero.

API#

Odin
// "The pass I am running in never resimulates." Scoped to the enclosing block,
// closes itself. Every query below asserts this was called.
pass_never_resims :: proc()

// The default 2D / 3D navigation map of the world `node` lives in.
map_2d :: proc(node: gd.Node) -> gd.Rid
map_3d :: proc(node: gd.Node) -> gd.Rid

// An optimized path across the node's default map ([] when unreachable or the
// map hasn't synced yet). The caller owns the slice.
path_2d :: proc(node: gd.Node, from, to: [3]f32, allocator := context.allocator) -> [][3]f32
path_3d :: proc(node: gd.Node, from, to: [3]f32, allocator := context.allocator) -> [][3]f32

// Query an already resolved map when several agents share it.
path_2d_on :: proc(nav_map: gd.Rid, from, to: [3]f32, allocator := context.allocator) -> [][3]f32
path_3d_on :: proc(nav_map: gd.Rid, from, to: [3]f32, allocator := context.allocator) -> [][3]f32

// Return the next waypoint. `idx` is the follower's cursor
// (start it at 0 per fresh path): waypoints within `reach` are consumed and
// never re-targeted — a stateless nearest-scan would walk you backwards to
// points you already passed. ok=false = the path is done (or empty).
next_point :: proc "contextless" (path: [][3]f32, idx: ^int, pos: [3]f32, reach: f32) -> (goal: [3]f32, ok: bool)

path_2d and path_3d use the node’s default world map, the map used by a NavigationRegion2D/3D added without a custom map. Resolving it requires three engine calls: node → viewport → world → navigation map. For a group of AI characters on the same map, resolve it once and pass the resulting RID to the _on query procedures.

Worked example: cavecrawl (examples/cavecrawl)#

Cavecrawl authors navigation with its floor scenes. In levels/level_1.tscn, a NavigationRegion2D contains a floor polygon around a rift. Every peer loads the scene, but only the host queries its navigation map.

The host’s AI update in scripts/host.odin runs in an authority-only pass. It opens the query scope and resolves the map once for the group:

Odin
@(private = "file")
cave_dwellers_think :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby) {
	knav.pass_never_resims()          // closes itself when this proc returns
	nav_map := knav.map_2d(self.owner) // resolved ONCE for the whole wave
	...
	pos = cave_dweller_walk(self, nav_map, pos, seen.pos)
}

A dweller queries a route, selects a waypoint, and advances toward it:

Odin
cave_dweller_walk :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, nav_map: gd.Rid, from, to: [3]f32) -> [3]f32 {
	path := knav.path_2d_on(nav_map, from, to, context.temp_allocator)
	idx := 0
	if goal, ok := knav.next_point(path, &idx, from, DWELLER_SPEED); ok {
		p, _ := kai.step_toward(from, goal, DWELLER_SPEED)
		return p
	}
	p, _ := kai.step_toward(from, to, DWELLER_SPEED) // empty path: walk the dumb way
	return p
}

The example makes three game-specific choices:

  • Query on each AI tick. It discards the path after the movement step, so the cursor starts at 0 and consumes the current snapped position. This avoids a separate path-cache invalidation policy when a floor changes or a successor resumes the host’s backed-up Dweller_Brain state. The cost is one map_get_path per agent per tick, at 20 Hz, for single-digit waves.
  • Choose a fallback for an empty path. The destination may be unreachable, or the map may not have synchronized after the floor entered the tree. Cavecrawl uses straight-line step_toward in that case. Another game may choose to wait and retry instead.
  • Check that navigation was used. The host prints CAVE_NAV_BENT once when a path contains an interior corner. The integration test requires that marker; visible movement alone would not establish that the navigation query produced a route around the rift.

The path is not replicated. The host streams the dweller’s x/y fields through the normal owner-state path described in kit/ai. Clients display those positions without running navigation queries.

Navigation constraints#

  • The query-scope check is an assertion. An unsupported query is not converted into an empty path, because an empty path is already a valid query result.
  • Regions synchronize at the NavigationServer’s physics cadence. A query made in the frame that adds a region may return an empty path. Repeated queries can wait for synchronization; a one-shot query must handle that initial delay (tests/kitnav waits 5 frames and retries).
  • The caller owns the returned slice. Use context.temp_allocator for a path discarded during the tick, or free an allocation that you retain.
  • Keep a cursor per follower and reset it to 0 for each new path. A stateless nearest-waypoint search can select points the follower has already passed.
  • Cavecrawl uses kai.step_away directly for fleeing. That operation chooses a direction, while a path query needs a destination. A later path home can start off the mesh: map_get_path snaps from to a walkable point.
  • 2D queries discard input z and return z = 0. Keep the [3]f32 convention consistent when sharing AI code between the 2D and 3D adapters.
  • Check reachability against the game’s progression rules. Cavecrawl leaves ledges north and south of the rift so enemies cannot remain stranded and block the floor-cleared condition.
